policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV renders a finite plural subject in 'that ye may provoke me,' distinguishing the ketiv הכעסוני ('ye provoke me') from the qere infinitival form הַכְעִיסֵנִי.
ASV 'And I will bring' does not distinguish the qere וְהֵבֵאתִי from the ketiv והבאיתי; no mapped textual note selects either spelling, so the base qere remains the fallback.
